The Evolution of Freedom In "Vansterdam" Special To Marijuananews

September 21, 1999

Even without an "Amsterdam Coffee House Hemporium" on the corner, the parallels between Vancouver and the Dutch city are obvious. Freedom is evolving in Vancouver in much the same way as it did in Holland twenty years ago. The current Dutch policy did not spring up over night as the result of some brilliant fiat. For starters, that is not the Dutch way.

See
Very Accurate Description of Dutch Cannabis Policies
On Front Page Of Canada’s National Newspaper!   Important!
and

Some of the pioneers in the Dutch marijuana business have been arrested many times. Unlike in DEAland, being arrested on repeated marijuana charges is not a disaster in Holland. That has also become the case in Vancouver.

The first "tolerated" sales in Holland were by "house dealers" at popular nightclubs, like the Melkweg, and at a few coffee shops, because "coffee shops" were not risking a valuable liquor license.

This will also be the way things will work in Vancouver. For now, there are only a few business places where smoking marijuana is tolerated. (People are almost never arrested here for simple possession, because the courts won’t prosecute.) There aren’t any house dealers, yet.

At the Amsterdam Coffee House Hemporium there is a poster on the door advertising comedy nights, with the notation at the bottom: "BYOB – Bring Your Own Bud." And that is not Budweiser!

It is around the corner from where Hemp BC used to be. The closing of Hemp BC after repeated raids was a demonstration of the current "limits of tolerance" in Vancouver.
See
Hemp BC And Cannabis Café To Close As A Result Of City Political Pressure;
Neighborhood Merchants Want Them To Stay. Protests Urged By Cannabis Culture.

Hemp BC founder Marc Emery is the sort of person who "pushes envelopes" in keeping with his libertarian philosophy. There is the old joke that you can always recognize a pioneer: They are the ones with the arrows in the back.

Marc Emery took a lot of arrows -- like Dennis Peron in San Francisco. Nonetheless, he seems undeterred. Marc is famous for being one of the most generous supporters of the marijuana reform movement. He has given thousands of dollars to support the Medical Marijuana Class Action suit in Philadelphia.

And others are benefiting from his work. Next door to the now closed Hemp BC is the very impressive "Blunt Bros. – A Respectable Joint." See www.bluntbros.com

It really reminds me of some of my favorite spots in Amsterdam, although the Dutch cannot afford to be so lavish in their use of space. Of course, there is no "house dealer." No weed menu. Instead, they have a sign that warns against selling "anything illegal." And they have to mean it.

Amusingly, Vancouver has an anti-tobacco-smoking policy, so Blunt Bros. has a smoking room up by the front door. However, I am told that the health police stop work at 4:30, which means that at 4:20 it is 4:20.

Blunt Bros. has a full page ad in the current High Times with the header: "Welcome to the Green Zone." It is a part of a cannabis consortium that sells seeds and even has a bed and breakfast in the hills just outside of Vancouver. It is called Mary Jane’s Hideaway.

They clearly understand business, but they also understand the political and social context, i. e. the realities of marijuana prohibition in North America. Having a social conscience and being politically aware is not incompatible with having business sense. Making social change requires all three, but knowing how hard to push is an art not a science.

Of course, business sense also makes it unlikely that Blunt Bros. will have the first house dealer in Vancouver. They have too much to lose. In any case, they are too late to be the first. There has already been a "coffee shop" that sold cannabis in Vancouver. Notice the past tense. The police closed it, but the owner has not yet been charged. He -- or someone else -- will push the envelope again. Sooner or later the arrests will stop, and it will be safe to sell small amounts of cannabis over the counter in coffee shops in Vansterdam.

That time is not too far distant. In the meantime, weed is everywhere… with one striking exception.

Ironically, The Bulldog – as the sign says of "Amsterdam and Vancouver" -- with its famous bulldog logo, does not allow any smoking of anything. As in Amsterdam, they have a liquor license. Here they cannot keep it and sell cannabis, yet.

Vancouver is so beautiful and the people are so friendly, that one does not need another excuse to visit. However, people from DEAland also enjoy the absence of fear. It is a subconscious memory of the freedom that we talk about but have not regained, yet.

Freedom is evolving in Vancouver and it is having an impact on the rest of Canada -- and on DEAland. The prohibitionists understand the threat.
See
Canadian Police Lie to The Canadian Media Who Lie To Their Readers
To Justify More Power Over the Canadian People To Please DEAland Narks
An Utterly Wretched Piece Of Pseudo-journalism

The anti-prohibitionists need to understand the opportunity better.
